record.field: Product Master — how products are organised
product master, catalogue, family, brand, form, sku, prd, identity

div.p: Every product is described by a few simple parts so the system can name it, give it a code, and group it with its relatives:

ul.li: Category — where it belongs (Animal Care ▸ Medicines, Feed ▸ Concentrate, Tools…).
Family — the generic item (Paracetamol, Cow Feed, Drill).
Brand — the maker (Cipla, Himalaya, Bosch, or "Local").
Form — the shape (Tablet, Syrup, Pellet) — or the Model for tools.
Strength, Pack size, Variant — the specifics (500 mg, 50 kg, Premium).

div.p: From these the system builds the SKU (the readable code on the label), a permanent internal code (PRD-…), and the barcode — automatically. See Create a product (guided) to do it, and the Product Master policy for the one rule that keeps the catalogue clean.

record.field: create product, new product, guided, wizard, sku preview, barcode preview, add product

div.p: Use Operations → Create Product (guided) for one product at a time. The screen fills itself in as you go:

ol.li: Category — pick it; the WMS Kind and which fields are required fill in automatically.
Family / Brand / Form — type to search. Not there yet? Pick Create and edit…, enter the Name + a short Code (e.g. Cipla → CIP), save — it's selected for you. No need to leave the screen.
Strength / Pack size / Variant — fill what applies (e.g. 500 mg, 10).
Watch the Preview box: the SKU (e.g. MED-PARA-CIP-TAB-500MG-10) and barcode update as you type. If a warning says the item already exists, adjust a field instead of making a duplicate.
Create (opens the new product) or Create & New (keep adding).

div.p: To load many products at once, use Configuration → Onboard Products instead. To put stock in, use Scan Receipt.

record.field: Product Master policy — keep the catalogue clean
policy, duplicate, family, brand, form, governance, naming, catalogue clean

div.p: One golden rule: a Family is the bare item — nothing else. The brand, form, strength, and pack are separate fields, never part of a Family / Brand / Form name.

ul.li: ❌ Do NOT create families like Paracetamol 500, Paracetamol Tablet, Cipla Paracetamol.
✅ Create the Family Paracetamol once; put 500 mg in Strength, Tablet in Form, Cipla in Brand.

div.p: One per concept: one Family per item, one Brand per maker, one Form per shape. Before adding a new one, type the first few letters — if it already exists, reuse it.
The system blocks exact case/spacing duplicates automatically (Cipla = CIPLA), but only you can avoid synonyms and granularity drift. Full details: the Product Master Creation Policy document.

record.field: family, molecule, generic, group, paracetamol, cow feed

div.p: A Family is the plain item, without brand or pack — Paracetamol, Cow Feed, Phenyl, Drill. Every brand, strength and pack of that item points at the one Family, so you can find all paracetamol in one place.
Example Cipla Paracetamol Tablet 500 mg and Sun Paracetamol Syrup 60 ml are two products, but the same Family: Paracetamol.
Each Family has a short code (Paracetamol → PARA) that becomes part of the SKU.

record.field: brand, manufacturer, maker, cipla, himalaya, bosch, local

div.p: The Brand is who makes the item — Cipla, Himalaya, Bosch, Amul, or Local for unbranded goods. One Brand per maker (don't make "Cipla" and "Cipla Ltd").
Each Brand has a short code (Cipla → CIP) used in the SKU.

record.field: Form / Model — the shape of the item
form, model, tablet, syrup, pellet, spray, dosage form, tool model

div.p: The Form is the physical shape — Tablet, Syrup, Injection, Powder, Pellet, Spray. For tools and spare parts it is the Model (e.g. Cordless 18 V).
The Form also suggests the unit: a Tablet is counted in Units, a Syrup measured in Litres, a Powder in kg. Each Form has a short code (Tablet → TAB) used in the SKU.

record.field: The structured SKU — reading the code
sku, structured sku, internal reference, code, read sku, segments

div.p: The SKU is the readable code on the label, built from the item's parts so you can read it at a glance:
MED-PARA-CIP-TAB-500MG-10 = Medicine · Paracetamol · Cipla · Tablet · 500 mg · pack of 10.

It is generated automatically when the product is created — you never type it. Two genuinely different items always get different SKUs; an exact repeat is blocked. (Simple items with no brand/family fall back to a short code like CONS-00042.)
For day-to-day scanning you usually scan the barcode, not type the SKU.

record.field: prd, internal code, permanent code, product id, identifier

div.p: Every product also has a permanent internal code like PRD-000145. Unlike the SKU (which is readable and could be regenerated before stock arrives), the PRD code is stamped once and never changes — even if the brand, category or name is edited.
It is the stable handle for audits, imports and history. You rarely need it day-to-day; it's there so a product can always be traced unambiguously.

record.field: Why the SKU and barcode lock after stock arrives
freeze, locked, sku locked, barcode locked, cannot change, archive recreate

div.p: Once a product has had stock, its SKU and barcode lock. By then the code is on printed labels and in the stock history, so changing it would break what's already on the shelf.
To "change" a locked product, archive it and create a new one. Before any stock arrives you can still fix it with Regenerate SKU from identity on the product form.

record.field: "SKU already exists" when creating a product
sku already exists, duplicate product, blocked, cannot create, near duplicate

div.p: This is the system protecting the catalogue — a product with the same Family + Brand + Form + Strength + Pack already exists, so it won't make a near-duplicate.

ul.li: If it's the same item, cancel and open the existing product (the message names it).
If it's genuinely different, change the field that differs — Brand, Variant, Pack size or Strength — and the SKU becomes distinct.

div.p: The system never auto-adds "-2"; it asks you to make the item properly distinct so the catalogue stays clean.
